Subject: Proposal: three-tier COLA approach for fully remote hires (US / EU / APAC)

Team —

Following our comp committee sync, attached is a first pass at a more granular remote pay "COLA" (cost-of-living adjustment) tiering model to reduce manual exceptions and speed offers. High level: create three country/region tiers (Standard, Elevated, Premium) tied to a composite index (Numbeo rent + Mercer expat index), with automated multipliers applied to base bands.

Why this: we keep seeing 1) long negotiation cycles for senior remote candidates across APAC/EU, and 2) frequent ad-hoc exceptions that go to People Ops and Finance. A principled tiering model should reduce exceptions and make offer math deterministic.

What's attached: COLA_Tiers_Q4_2026.xlsx — includes: tier definitions, sample adjustments for RD IC/PM bands, and a list of markets assigned to each tier. benchmark_notes_Numbeo_Mercer.pdf summarizes data sources and methodology.

Key asks:
- Please review the thresholds and market assignments (sheet: "Tier map").
- We need agreement on whether Premium-tier approvals (any delta > +12% vs US baseline) require VP People + Finance sign-off or whether manager + PeopleOps is sufficient.
- Can Recruiting start using the tiered offer templates for roles that are approved at manager+PeopleOps level?

Proposed execution path: 1) PeopleOps validates benchmarks and publishes official tier table; 2) Recruiting immediately uses templates for Standard/Elevated; 3) Premium requires a short approval ticket in Jira (PRIORITY: <24h SLAs).

Notes: I intentionally used a composite index rather than pure GDP per capita to better reflect everyday cost pressure (rent + grocery + expat services). For small markets with thin data, I flagged them for manual review rather than automated assignment.

Attachment: COLA_Tiers_Q4_2026.xlsx (xlsx, 39KB)
Attachment: benchmark_notes_Numbeo_Mercer.pdf (pdf, 18KB)

Thanks — would like a sign-off path by EOD Thursday so recruiting can pilot on next week's offer batch.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Global GTM Recruiting
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: three-tier COLA approach for fully remote hires (US / EU / APAC)

Vanessa — thanks for the clear writeup and the model. Quick read and a few redlines below.

1) I like the three-tier simplification. One ask: can we preserve a small discretionary buffer at offer time (+/- 3%) for managers to close top-of-funnel senior candidates without escalating? If we require Jira for anything > 2% we'll still slow things down.

2) Premium-tier scope appears to capture London and SF as Premium, but Madrid and Dublin are currently Elevated in the sheet; please double-check Dublin — cost of living moved quickly this year and it might belong in Premium.

3) For EU cross-border payroll complexity: if we set a hard multiplier, remind Finance we may need an extra 4–6 week lead time for contracting in certain EU jurisdictions (we should call out Belgium/Netherlands as special cases).

4) Approvals: propose this split — Standard: manager sign-off; Elevated: manager + PeopleOps; Premium: manager + PeopleOps + Finance (VP People optional for headcount > 2 in same quarter). That keeps most offers from going to leadership.

I've annotated the sheet (see "Laura_comments" tab) with inline notes. Will loop Maya for regional market edits.

— Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations (Comp & Benefits)
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa / Laura / Marcus —

Thanks for the deck and the transparent methodology. We ran the tier map against our own Mercer/Numbeo blend and have three recommendations:

1) Replace the raw Numbeo rent series with a 6-month trailing median to smooth one-off spikes (important for small cities).
2) For APAC, include a currency-volatility adjustment for markets where FX swings > 8% YoY; that prevents mid-quarter surprises for hiring managers.
3) For payroll complexity, we recommend codifying a "time-to-contract" label in the sheet (Fast / Standard / Extended). That will let Recruiting pick markets that can close in the hiring cadence required.

We can accept the approval thresholds Laura suggested. One operational ask: can Redwood provide a single Slack channel + a short Jira ticket template that us and Finance can watch for Premium approvals? That will reduce turnaround.

Attachment: vendor_tiering_notes.pdf (pdf, 12KB)

Best,
PeopleOps Consulting (on behalf of Redwood engagement)

All — quick operational decision from my side: approved to pilot the tiering framework starting Monday for the following queues: Senior IC (L4-L6) and Product managers. Implementation notes:

- Recruiting: use the Standard/Elevated templates as-is. For Premium, submit the short Jira ticket (template in related links) and tag PeopleOps + Finance.
- PeopleOps: please finalize the tier map with the 6-month trailing rent median and add the Time-to-Contract column as recommended.
- Finance: I'll inform CFO that Premium approvals will be routed to Finance reviewer; Marcus will escalate to VP People only if headcount > 2 in the same quarter.

Let's monitor offer acceptance delta for the pilot cohort and reconvene in three weeks. Thanks Vanessa for driving this.
